messages:
maya: Heads-up: planning tenant-id swap + PK type change tonight 03:00 UTC. Backfill will populate new pk col for all tenants. main risk: orphaned rows if the backfill is interrupted or a partial shard finishes. need pin/version and rollback plan.

oliver: +1. do we want to pin api servers to the pre-swap tag during the backfill window? also: which tenants are low-risk canary targets?

deploybot: maintenance slot reserved: 2024-09-16 03:00-03:30 UTC for migration job tenant-swap-20240916. canary at 02:45 UTC. notify: #eng-oncall and #prod-ops.

emma: Can we shard the backfill by tenant id ranges (small canary set first)? also need an escape hatch cutoff: e.g. abort if backfill throughput drops >75% vs baseline or lock contention > p95 200ms.

jon: Propose concrete holdpoint: pause at 10% overall progress and validate row counts + FK integrity. Abort criteria: 1) any orphaned rows observed, 2) sustained backfill < 20 rows/s for >5m, 3) >1% error rate.

maya: Sounds good. baseline expectation ~150 rows/s across workers. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tenant-swap-backfill (add preflight checklist). I'll own canary.

lena: Rollback plan (short): 
- flip feature flag `tenant_swap_enabled=false`
- pin services: set deployment tag to `v1.4.2-pre-swap` via k8s rollout pause OR `kubectl set image ... --record`
- if data corruption suspected: restore snapshot created before migration: `pg_restore -d prod --clean snapshot_before_swap.dump` (note: single-transaction restore may take time)
Keep DB read-only routing for the window until verified.

oliver: Also add smoke tests post-canary: create tenant, write/read, verify old pk still resolves, run `SELECT count(*) FROM new_pk_table WHERE migrated = true LIMIT 1` on canary tenant.

sre-oncall: I will watch lock metrics and CPU. Query to monitor long locks: `SELECT pid, query, now()-pg_stat_activity.query_start AS age FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle' AND now()-pg_stat_activity.query_start > interval '5 seconds';` will alert if >5 long queries.

deploybot: Canary scheduled: 02:45 UTC for tenant range [1000-1099]. will report progress to thread.

emma: Add to release notes: brief what changed (PK type swap), impact (short maintenance), rollback steps, post-checklist. I'll create PR for notes and post link here before start.

maya: Final checklist I have: backups ok (yes), snapshot created (yes), preflight smoke passed (yes), alerting in place (yes), rollbacks staged (yes). I'll be in #prod-ops at 02:30.

deploybot: 02:50 UTC update: canary started. backfill rate ~120 rows/s, no lock spikes, errors 0.2%. logs: `worker-3: processed 720 rows in 6s`

jon: good to see numbers. holding to 10% checkpoint. abort if drops below 20 rows/s or error >1%.

deploybot: 03:05 UTC: canary paused by operator: detected stuck shard on worker-7 -> logs show `ERROR: deadlock detected while updating new_pk_table` and automatic pause triggered.

maya: Pausing rollout. we'll rollback canary only. good catch.

lena: Rollback steps for canary only: 
1) set `tenant_swap_enabled=false` feature flag for tenants 1000-1099
2) terminate backfill jobs for those shards: `pkill -f tenant-swap-1000-1099`
3) validate FK integrity with `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM new_pk_table WHERE tenant BETWEEN 1000 AND 1099 AND fk_ref IS NULL;`
Note: full snapshot restore NOT required unless we see orphaned rows > 0. restoring snapshot timeline estimate: 30-90 minutes depending on size.

emma: I'll open a postmortem stub and schedule follow-up slot tomorrow 04:00 UTC to re-run with safer batching and lower concurrency. Also propose RFC to change backfill algorithm to idempotent upserts and smaller transaction windows.

maya: Thanks all. we'll keep this thread updated. rolling the canary back now and documenting root cause. closing active ops for tonight; will re-schedule with improved plan. :white_check_mark:
